title: After-hours places and Central Avenue nightlife
summary: They name private houses and after-hours spots like Lovejoy's, Jack's Basket Room and Stuff Crouch's where musicians stayed until late morning.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: When you would hang out all night, where all would you go?

Yeah, Vernon and Central. And then there were several other after-hours places. I can't think of some of the people's names. But you know, the town was full of Jazz, because all the bands used to come here, and all of the movie stars hung out on Central Avenue because that's where the Jazz was happening.
Well, in those days as soon as the regular gig was up, then everybody went to those places and...
Then the music got really exciting, right?

Late morning. We might get in there until 2 or 3 in the morning and hang out until almost mid-day; you know, it might be 10 o'clock or 12 o'clock in the day. Then we'd go home and sleep. But when you're young, that's fun. You don't even get tired.
Jack's Basket Room. Yeah, you remember some of those names.
I remember some of those places, right. Stuff Crouch's Backstage.
Stuff Crouch's Backstage. Milo-Mo(?) was another place...
No, it wasn't after-hours. That was over on Western Avenue.
